en: His brothers stand in the palace of Egypt, begging for grain.
Their families are hungry.
Their goods are poor.
And they plead with the man in charge of Egypt's storehouses: give us full measure...
and be charitable to us.
He knows every one of them.
They have no idea who he is.
Years ago, these same men threw a little boy into the bottom of a well...
and told their father a wolf had eaten him.
That boy is the man standing in front of them.
This is the complete story of Hazrat Yusuf, alayhis salaam, from Surah Yusuf.
Allah calls it the best of stories.
It begins... with a dream.
A boy comes to his father, the Prophet Yaqub, alayhis salaam.
"O my father, I have seen eleven stars, and the sun, and the moon...
I saw them prostrating to me."
His father understood at once.
This was no ordinary dream.
And he knew his other sons.
"O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, or they will contrive against you a plan.
Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy."
Then he gave him good news: your Lord will choose you, and teach you the meaning of dreams, and complete His favour upon you.
A dream of honour.
A warning of danger.
And the danger was already closer than anyone knew.
His brothers were jealous.
"Yusuf and his brother are more beloved to our father than we are," they said.
Some of them wanted to kill him.
One said: do not kill him...
throw him into the bottom of the well.
So they asked their father to send Yusuf out with them tomorrow, to eat well and play.
Hazrat Yaqub said: "It saddens me that you should take him...
and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are not watching."
Without knowing it, he had just handed them their excuse.
They took him out, and together they put him into the bottom of the well.
And there, in the dark, alone, Allah sent him a promise.
"You will surely inform them, someday, about this affair of theirs...
while they do not perceive."
That night, the brothers came home to their father, weeping.
"O our father, we went racing each other, and left Yusuf with our things...
and a wolf ate him."
And they brought his shirt, with false blood on it.
But their father saw through it.
"Rather, your souls have enticed you to something.
So patience is most fitting."
Patience is most fitting. Sabrun jameel.
Remember those words... because he will say them again.
Out in the desert, a caravan passed.
They sent a man to draw water, and he let down his bucket...
"Good news! Here is a boy!"
They hid him away as merchandise.
And they sold him for a cheap price... a few dirhams.
To them, he was worth almost nothing.
The man in Egypt who bought him told his wife: "Make his stay comfortable.
Perhaps we will adopt him as a son."
A boy thrown away by his own brothers...
was now living in one of the great houses of Egypt.
And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
Yusuf grew into a man, and Allah gave him judgment and knowledge.
But that same house was about to bring his hardest test.
The wife of al-Aziz, the woman of that house, tried to seduce him.
She closed the doors and said: "Come."
He said: "I seek the refuge of Allah.
He is my master, who has made good my residence.
Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
And he saw the proof of his Lord.
Allah turned evil away from him, for he was one of Allah's chosen servants.
They both raced to the door. She grabbed him...
and tore his shirt from the back.
And at the door... stood her husband.
At once she blamed him, and demanded prison, or a painful punishment.
Yusuf said: "It was she who sought to seduce me."
Then a witness from her own family said: look at the shirt.
If it is torn from the front, she is telling the truth.
If it is torn from the back... she has lied.
They looked. The shirt was torn from the back.
His second shirt. The first one told a lie about him.
This one told the truth.
But the story spread.
The women of the city said: the wife of al-Aziz is chasing her servant.
She is clearly in error.
When she heard their talk, she invited them to a banquet, and gave each of them a knife.
Then she told Yusuf to come out before them.
When they saw him, they were so stunned that they cut their own hands.
"Perfect is Allah! This is not a man.
This is none but a noble angel."
She said: "That is the one you blamed me for."
And if he would not obey her, he would be imprisoned.
Now the pressure came from every side.
And Yusuf turned to the only One who could help.
"My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me."
His Lord answered him, and turned their plan away from him.
And even after they had seen every sign of his innocence...
they decided to put him in prison anyway.
An innocent man, locked away for doing what was right.
Two young men entered the prison with him, and each had a dream.
One saw himself pressing wine.
The other saw birds eating bread from his head.
"Tell us what it means," they said, "we see that you are one of those who do good."
Even in a prison cell, people could see it.
But before he answered, Yusuf told them about Allah.
"O my two companions of prison, are separate lords better...
or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?"
Then he gave the meaning.
One of them would serve his master again.
The other would not survive.
To the one he knew would go free, he said: "Mention me to your master."
But Satan made him forget.
And Yusuf remained in prison... for several years.
Then one night, the king of Egypt saw a dream that shook him.
"I have seen seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain, and others dry.
O eminent ones, explain to me my vision."
His advisers had no answer.
"A mixture of false dreams," they said.
And suddenly, the man who had been freed remembered.
After all those years... he remembered Yusuf.
He went to the prison.
"Yusuf, O man of truth, explain this to us."
Yusuf did not bargain for his freedom.
He simply gave them the answer, and a plan.
For seven years, plant as usual.
What you harvest, leave in its ears, except a little that you eat.
Then seven hard years will come, and eat up what you stored.
Then a year will come with rain, and the people will be relieved.
A forgotten prisoner had just saved a nation from famine.
The king said: "Bring him to me."
But when the messenger came, Yusuf would not leave.
"Go back to your master, and ask him about the women who cut their hands."
He wanted his name cleared before he walked out.
The king questioned the women.
And the wife of al-Aziz confessed: "Now the truth has become evident.
It was I who sought to seduce him, and he is of the truthful."
The king said: "Bring him to me."
And when he spoke with him: "Today you are established with us, and trusted."
Yusuf said: "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land.
Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."
From the bottom of a well... to a slave... to a prisoner...
to the man in charge of the food of Egypt.
We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
The famine came, just as he had said.
And it reached far beyond Egypt...
all the way to his father's land.
One day, a group of travellers came to buy grain.
Yusuf looked at them...
and knew them instantly. His brothers.
They had no idea who he was.
He gave them their supplies and said: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father.
If you do not bring him, there will be no measure for you from me."
At home, Hazrat Yaqub did not want to let his younger son go.
"Should I entrust you with him, as I entrusted you with his brother before?"
But they needed food, and he let him go.
When they arrived, Yusuf took his brother aside and told him quietly: "I am your brother.
So do not despair over what they used to do."
Then he put the king's golden measuring cup into his brother's bag.
As the caravan set off, a voice called out: "O caravan, indeed you are thieves!"
The bags were searched, one by one.
And the cup came out...
from the bag of the youngest brother, Binyamin.
The brothers said: "If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before."
They were lying about Yusuf, to Yusuf's face.
He kept it within himself, and said nothing.
They begged him: our father is an old man.
Take one of us instead.
He refused.
And they went home...
to tell their father he had lost another son.
When they told him, Hazrat Yaqub said the same words he had said all those years ago.
"Rather, your souls have enticed you to something.
So patience is most fitting."
Sabrun jameel. Again.
But this time he added: "Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together."
He turned away and said: "Oh, my sorrow over Yusuf."
His grief was so deep that his eyes turned white.
And still, he held it in.
His sons told him to stop, before grief destroyed him.
And he answered with one of the most beautiful lines in the Quran.
"I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.
And I know from Allah that which you do not know."
Then he told them: "O my sons, go and find out about Yusuf and his brother.
And despair not of relief from Allah."
After all these years...
he still had not given up.
So the brothers returned to Egypt, and stood once more before its ruler.
"O Aziz, hardship has touched us and our family.
Give us full measure, and be charitable to us."
And the man in front of them asked one question.
"Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother, when you were ignorant?"
How could this stranger know?
"Are you... are you indeed Yusuf?"
"I am Yusuf, and this is my brother.
Allah has been gracious to us.
Whoever fears Allah and is patient...
Allah does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost."
The promise from the bottom of the well had come true.
They said: "By Allah, Allah has preferred you over us, and we have been sinners."
He had the power to punish them.
He had every reason to.
Instead, he said:
"No blame will there be upon you today.
Allah will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
Then he gave them his shirt.
"Take this shirt of mine and cast it over the face of my father.
He will see again.
And bring me all your family."
His third shirt. The first carried a lie.
The second carried the truth.
This one would carry healing.
As the caravan left Egypt, far away, an old man said: "I can smell Yusuf...
if you would not think me weak in mind."
When the bearer of good news arrived, he cast the shirt over his face...
and he could see again.
"Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?"
Then the whole family travelled to Egypt.
Yusuf raised his parents up onto the throne...
and they all bowed down before him.
The sun. The moon. And eleven stars.
"O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before.
My Lord has made it reality."
And he said: "He was good to me when He took me out of prison."
Notice what he did not say.
He did not say "when He took me out of the well."
Even now, he would not shame his brothers.
A well. A slave market. A locked door. A prison. Years of waiting.
Every one of them was a step towards the throne.
Allah says at the end of this surah: "There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding."
So when your life feels like the bottom of a well... remember Yusuf.
Patience is most fitting.
And never despair of relief from Allah.
